---
title: "NFL Play-by-Play (2009-2016): Static Exploration"
author: "Will Carter"
---

## Purpose

This file explores the cleaned NFL play-by-play data before building the Shiny app.
The tables and plots will be accessed on the app's data exploration tab.

The data covers every pass, run, and sack from the 2009-2016 regular and postseasons. 
The dataset is sourced from [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/maxhorowitz/nflplaybyplay2009to2016).
`data_process.R` cleans it and saves it to `app/nfl_pbp.rds`.

```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

nfl <- readRDS("app/nfl_pbp.rds")
glimpse(nfl)
```

## contingency tables

### one-way tables

How often teams pass, run, or get sacked:

```{r one-way-play-type}
table(nfl$play_type)
```

Where plays start on the field:

```{r one-way-field-zone}
table(nfl$field_zone)
```

### two-way tables

Play type by down. Teams run most on 1st down and they pass most on 3rd down.

```{r two-way-down}
table(nfl$down, nfl$play_type)
```

The same table as proportions:

```{r two-way-down-prop}
round(prop.table(table(nfl$down, nfl$play_type), margin = 1), 3)
```

Pass length by pass location. Most passes are short, and fewer go over the middle:

```{r two-way-pass}
table(nfl$pass_length, nfl$pass_location)
```

## numeric summaries by group

Yards gained and EPA by down and play type:

```{r summary-down-type}
nfl |>
  group_by(down, play_type) |>
  summarize(
    n            = n(),
    mean_yards   = mean(yards_gained),
    median_yards = median(yards_gained),
    sd_yards     = sd(yards_gained),
    mean_epa     = mean(epa, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Air yards on passes by pass length and outcome:

```{r summary-air-yards}
nfl |>
  filter(play_type == "Pass", !is.na(pass_length)) |>
  group_by(pass_length, pass_outcome) |>
  summarize(
    n                = n(),
    mean_air_yards   = mean(air_yards, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_air_yards = median(air_yards, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_air_yards     = sd(air_yards, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

Win probability by game situation:

```{r summary-win-prob}
nfl |>
  group_by(game_situation) |>
  summarize(
    n         = n(),
    mean_wp   = mean(win_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_wp = median(win_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_wp     = sd(win_prob, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

## plots

### play type by down

```{r plot-bar-down}
ggplot(nfl, aes(x = down, fill = play_type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(
    title = "Play Type by Down",
    x = "Down",
    y = "Number of plays",
    fill = "Play type"
  )
```

Runs are better than passes on 1st down, but passing takes over on 2nd and 3rd down. 

### 2. distribution of yards gained

```{r plot-hist-yards}
nfl |>
  filter(play_type != "Sack", between(yards_gained, -10, 40)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = yards_gained, fill = play_type)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity") +
  labs(
    title = "Yards Gained on Passes and Runs",
    subtitle = "Plays gaining between -10 and 40 yards",
    x = "Yards gained",
    y = "Number of plays",
    fill = "Play type"
  )
```

Runs center around 1-5 yards. Passes have a big spike at 0 (incompletions) and a longer right tail.

### 3. EPA by field zone (box plot)

```{r plot-box-epa}
nfl |>
  filter(!is.na(epa)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = field_zone, y = epa, fill = play_type)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.1) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-4, 4)) +
  labs(
    title = "Expected Points Added by Field Position and Play Type",
    x = "Field zone",
    y = "EPA",
    fill = "Play type"
  )
```

Sacks are costly everywhere. The spread of EPA widens in the red zone, where a single play can mean a touchdown.

### 4. Air yards vs. EPA on passes (scatter plot)

```{r plot-scatter-air}
set.seed(558)
nfl |>
  filter(play_type == "Pass", !is.na(pass_outcome), !is.na(epa)) |>
  slice_sample(n = 5000) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = air_yards, y = epa, color = pass_outcome)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Air Yards vs. EPA on Pass Attempts",
    subtitle = "Random sample of 5,000 passes",
    x = "Air yards (distance the ball traveled past the line of scrimmage)",
    y = "EPA",
    color = "Outcome"
  )
```

Completions gain more value the farther downfield they are completed. Incompletions 
sit at a small negative EPA irrespective of distance. The large negative outliers are mostly interceptions.

### 5. pass rate by quarter and game situation

```{r plot-facet-pass-rate}
nfl |>
  group_by(quarter, game_situation) |>
  summarize(pass_rate = mean(play_type != "Run"), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = quarter, y = pass_rate, fill = quarter)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ game_situation) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(
    title = "Pass Rate by Quarter and Score",
    subtitle = "Sacks count as pass plays",
    x = "Quarter",
    y = "Share of plays that are passes"
  )
```

Passing rates are similar across scores early on. In the 4th quarter they split.
Teams that are being outscored pass 77% of the time, while leading teams drop to
about 38% as to run out the clock.

### 6. pass rate by down and distance

Each tile shows how often teams pass in a given down-and-distance situation.

```{r plot-heatmap-down-dist}
nfl |>
  mutate(distance = cut(ydstogo,
                        breaks = c(0, 2, 5, 9, 10, 15, Inf),
                        labels = c("1-2", "3-5", "6-9", "10", "11-15", "16+"))) |>
  group_by(down, distance) |>
  summarize(pass_rate = mean(play_type != "Run"), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = distance, y = down, fill = pass_rate)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pass_rate, accuracy = 1)), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f7fbff", high = "#08519c",
                      labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +
  labs(
    title = "How Often Teams Pass, by Down and Distance",
    x = "Yards to go",
    y = "Down",
    fill = "Pass rate"
  )
```

Short yardage leans toward runs on every down. On 3rd and 4th down with 3+ yards to go, teams pass 80-90% of the time.

### 7. EPA by pass length and location (heatmap)

```{r plot-heatmap-pass-epa}
nfl |>
  filter(play_type == "Pass", !is.na(pass_length), !is.na(pass_location)) |>
  group_by(pass_length, pass_location) |>
  summarize(mean_epa = mean(epa, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pass_location, y = pass_length, fill = mean_epa)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(mean_epa, 2)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#b2182b", mid = "white", high = "#2166ac",
                       midpoint = 0) +
  labs(
    title = "Average EPA by Pass Length and Location",
    x = "Pass location",
    y = "Pass length",
    fill = "Mean EPA"
  )
```

Deep passes over the middle return the most value on average, despite being thrown the least.
